<p class="cycle-role">Observed outcomes, their distribution, and evidence that informs subsequent decisions.</p>

<p class="page-deck"><strong>What does climate action change, for whom, where and over what period?</strong></p>

We study how climate action affects health, equity, social cohesion and other dimensions of wellbeing, including how benefits, burdens and risks are distributed across populations and places.

::: {.notice}
**Part of a connected learning cycle.** Projects and cities may enter at different points. Evidence about consequences can revise judgements about existing knowledge and where new evidence matters.
:::

## Questions the lab investigates

- How are benefits, burdens and risks distributed across populations and places?
- What health, equity, social-cohesion and local economic consequences occur over time?
- How should place-based appraisal represent uncertainty, adverse effects and uneven outcomes?

## Analytical boundary

- Assuming that all consequences of climate action are positive or evenly distributed.
- Promotional co-benefit claims without an identifiable evidence basis.
